LeBron James (born December 30, 1984) is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes ever. He played high school ball at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School in Akron, Ohio, and was drafted first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2003.

**Career Highlights**

| Team | Years | Key Achievements |
|------|-------|------------------|
| **Cleveland Cavaliers** | 2003–2010, 2014–2018 | NBA Finals appearances (2007, 2015), MVP awards (2009, 2010). |
| **Miami Heat** | 2010–2014 | Two consecutive championships (2012, 2013); two Finals MVPs. |
| **Los Angeles Lakers** | 2018–present | Championship (2020), Finals MVP (2020). |

He has earned four regular‑season MVP titles (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013), four NBA Finals MVP honors (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020), and has been selected to numerous All‑NBA teams. Off the court he’s known for philanthropy—especially his “I Promise” program aimed at helping children from low-income families—and for being a prominent voice on social justice issues.

In addition to his playing career, LeBron has built a media empire with ventures such as SpringHill Entertainment, producing films and television shows, and co‑founding Uninterrupted, a platform giving athletes control over their own stories.
